title: Sensor triage
lede: Every reading is judged against its asset's normal range, in context rather than as a raw number. A real anomaly dispatches maintenance with the reading attached; routine telemetry rolls up into aggregates.
if_down: Every reading is flagged for a person. None rolls up unseen, and none is dispatched without a judgment.

stages.title: Parse the body
stages.text: The input already parses JSON bodies. This stage only parses a body that arrives as a string, so both shapes become the same object before anything else touches it.

stages.title: Attach the baseline and arrival time
stages.text: Adds the asset class's normal operating limits next to the reading so Jev judges deviation in context, plus received_at.

stages.title: Start the latency timer
stages.text: Stores the current time in message metadata. The message itself does not change, so the output below equals the input; the timer is read after Jev answers.

stages.title: Ask Jev
stages.text: One request carries the record and the questions below. The answer is merged under `jev` with the model name and the round trip in milliseconds. If Jev cannot be reached, the catch block substitutes an empty answer set and every rule below falls to its default branch, so nothing is guessed.

stages.title: Decide where it goes
stages.text: A dispatch likelihood of 0.8 or more dispatches maintenance. Otherwise an anomaly score of 2 or more, or no answer from Jev, flags the reading for a person. Everything else rolls up.

stages.title: Write to a queue
stages.text: Dispatch, flagged and rollup are separate JSONL files under data/jev-sensor-triage/.
